messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: P0 - inference-gateway 5xx surge - service=inference-gateway-prod
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty | Incident created: INC-2026-9998 — urgency=high — trigger=5xx rate > 7% in 2m
maria_g: I got the page. which region is hot?
sam_k: us-east-1 showing spike, p95 token latency also up a bit. grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/inf/inference-gateway?from=now-10m
leila_ops: grabbing traces now, will paste any errors.
jon_s: early look — lots of `kv-cache miss -> fallback` followed by `incompatible-kernel` traces on a handful of GPU workers. could be a kernel-selection mismatch after last-night's runtime tweak.
mina_oncall: we rolled a small runtime tweak at 03:15 UTC touching kernel heuristics, confirmed.
sam_k: primary (sam_k) was paged at 4289990000 and didn't ack quickly (driving). PD auto-escalated per policy to secondary.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation notice: primary unacknowledged >2m. Notifying secondary: leila_ops
leila_ops: acked via PD at 4289990018 :white_check_mark: starting triage. quick log tail: `kubectl -n prod logs deploy/inference-gateway --since=15m | grep ERROR | tail -n 80`
leila_ops: stack shows repeated `CUDAError: kernel mismatch` and then `ERROR kv-cache miss -> fallback failed: variant-incompatible`
erin_m: support reporting inbound tickets: several Dedicated tenants reporting streaming reconnects and 502s — ticket TCK-9102 created.
maria_g: can we apply a targeted routing override to avoid the quantized variant in us-east-1 as a temporary mitigation? That should reduce failures quickly.
jon_s: yes, control-plane supports atomic routing override per-region. Endpoint: `POST /api/v1/routing/override` Body: `{"region":"us-east-1","variant_preference":{"quantized":false}}`
leila_ops: executing now: ```curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/override -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"region":"us-east-1","variant_preference":{"quantized":false}}'```
leila_ops: override applied. propagation time ~30-45s. monitoring.
sam_k: error rate down 7% -> 2.6% in last 90s. latency normalizing for routed traffic.
pagerduty-bot: Incident assigned to leila_ops at 4289990035
mina_oncall: checking infra nodes — node-gpu-22 shows dmesg entries with `OOM killed process` ~18m before current time. could be related to kv-cache corruption.
jon_s: if KV cache was corrupted on restart/OOM, requests will miss and fallback path could attempt an incompatible kernel. Cordoning the suspect node and draining may help.
leila_ops: cordon/drain node-gpu-22: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-22 && kubectl drain node-gpu-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — starting now.
erin_m: support update: told impacted tenants we applied temporary routing override; asking them to retry streams. Will update ticket every 15m.
alex_p: I'm manager on rotation — watching this thread. If secondary unack or mitigation fails, PD will page me per policy. Keep me posted.
leila_ops: drain succeeded. node shows repeated `CudaDriver: device lost` logs. I'll schedule a reprovision/reimage.
sam_k: reimage queued — ETA 9m. rollback path for runtime tweak exists but has perf caveats; estimate ~12m to rollback and warm. prefer keep override while we reimage and monitor.
jon_s: agree. add an alert that will page manager if 5xx > 5% for 4m. we don't want silent escalation later.
leila_ops: set PD escalation rule watch: if 5xx > 5% for 4m -> escalate manager at 4289990201.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy: secondary acked at 4289990036. Manager escalate condition configured.
maria_g: customer impact summary for support: "Small cohort of Dedicated tenants in us-east-1 experienced transient 5xxs and streaming disconnects starting ~4289990000. We applied a per-region routing override to deprioritize quantized variants that reduced 5xxs. Node-gpu-22 was cordoned and reimaged. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem."
erin_m: support has updated ticket TCK-9102 with that messaging. Customers thanked for patience; no data loss reported.
leila_ops: reimage completed, bringing node back in with 10% traffic. watching logs for `device lost` or `incompatible-kernel` events. so far clean.
jon_s: we should add a metric to detect variant mismatch attempts (count of `fallback->incompatible-kernel` events) and alert earlier. Will add to backlog.
sam_k: rolling off override slowly in 20m if there are no regressions. Meanwhile I'll run the runtime tweak in a canary environment with forced quantized variants to validate kernel-selection compatibility.
alex_p: note on PD behavior — if secondary briefly loses network or mobile DND, the manager will be paged. We should check PD schedule windows to avoid noisy escalations during known commute hours. Filing follow-up: PD policy audit.
leila_ops: current error rate stabilized at ~1.8% across region. mitigation looks effective. leaving routing override for another 30m and monitoring.
maria_g: incident P0 duration so far: 26m. recommendation: keep mitigation, validate in staging, avoid immediate rollback to prod. postmortem owners: jon_s (RCA), leila_ops (ops remediation), erin_m (customer comms).
erin_m: posting final customer-facing note and closing support loop for impacted tenants.
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-9998 — status updated to Mitigated (monitoring) at 4289990125 — notes saved to incident log.
maria_g: thanks everyone. add your exact commands, logs, and timestamps into postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/postmortems/INC-2026-9998 — retain blameless language.
leila_ops: adding runbook snippet: "If quantized-fallback causes 5xx: apply regional routing override -> cordon+drain suspect GPU node -> reimage -> monitor -> only rollback runtime tweak if errors recur after other mitigations."
jon_s: follow-ups: instrument kernel-selection mismatch metric, add CI test for quantized/non-quant compatibility, PD schedule audit.
maria_g: closing notes: incident remained P0 for 28m; small number of Dedicated tenants affected; secondary handled triage and mitigations; manager remained on standby and paged for awareness only. postmortem due EOD. Thanks team :heart:
